messages.preview: The clone-around fallback fails when the workspace's PARENT is unwritable — let me check if that's realistic on the actual runner and try to simulate the true mount-stub (EBUSY) case:

blocks.text:
IMPORTANT FINDING! The clone-around-stub fallback has a real bug:

When the workspace dir cannot be MOVED ASIDE because its PARENT directory is not writable (`mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE"` fails with Permission denied on the parent), the script falls into the clone-around path, choosing `CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"` — a SIBLING in the SAME unwritable parent. Creating that sibling fails with `mkdir: Permission denied` (git clone can't create the target dir) → the whole checkout FAILS.

But wait — is this scenario realistic on the actual runner? On the self-hosted box, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` = `<runner>/_work/<repo>/<repo>` and the parent `<repo>` is owned by the runner user — writable. The move-aside would only fail there because of a mount-held path issue: rename(2) of a directory CONTAING a mount point fails with EBUSY even with writable parent. In THAT realistic case, creating `workspace.checkout` in the writable parent succeeds, and the clone-around works.

So the failure mode I simulated (unwritable parent) is not the realistic failure mode. Let me re-simulate with the REALISTIC stub: a directory that can't be deleted/moved because it's a mount point. I can't create real mounts without privileges... but I CAN simulate EBUSY by making the leftover path a mount-like obstacle: use `chattr +i`? Needs CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE — may work as root in this container? Let me check if I'm root.

Actually, a simpler realistic simulation: make the workspace itself contain an undeletable entry AND the parent writable but... mv of the workspace dir: rename(2) needs write perm on parent only (plus the dir must not be ancestor of the cwd etc.). With parent writable and a leftover chmod-000 dir inside, mv of the whole workspace SUCCEEDS (dir modes don't block rename).           if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then

            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi

            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"

            while IFS= read -r entry; do

              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi

            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

+// gh-1600 — the daily-publish testflight leg failed twice over:

+//   L1-routing      `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the
+//                   GENERIC `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which
+//                   also matches the Linux self-hosted box's advertised
+//                   labels — the iOS job ran on Linux and died with
+//                   `bundle: command not found` (exit 127) at Install
+//                   fastlane (run 38516656653; the 2026-10-15 night run
+//                   additionally hit `security: command not found`).
+//   L1-isolation    bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared
+//                   self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → jobs/
+//                   fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, trial dirs bind-mounted into
+//                   task containers), so the mobile legs' bare
+//                   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers
+//                   and failed the checkout before any build step.
+//
+// Static workflow-shape asserts (the "workflow-shape test never-again"
+// pattern of workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart / release_hygiene_test.dart):
+//
+//   AC1  every self-hosted job in the macOS publish legs (build-mobile.yml,
+//        build-macos.yml) pins the UNIQUE macOS label `macos-m5` — the
+//        fa-m5-1 registration (gh-1005: the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS M5
+//        runner) — and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels that the
+//        Linux box also satisfies.
+//   AC2  a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same box
+//        cannot break the checkout: bench-harbor writes its job output
+//        OUTSIDE $GITHUB_WORKSPACE ($RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs) and tears its
+//        docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir, and the
+//        three mirror-checkout jobs clean the shared workspace
+//        log-and-prune (a stale unremovable path moves aside / the clone
+//        works around it instead of failing).

+
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+import 'package:yaml/yaml.dart';
+
+String read(String path) => File(path).readAsStringSync();
+
+YamlMap jobsOf(String workflowPath) =>
+    loadYaml(read(workflowPath))['jobs'] as YamlMap;
+
+/// The `run` script of the named step in the named job of the workflow.
+String checkoutScriptOf(String workflowPath, String job, String stepName) {
+  final steps = (jobsOf(workflowPath)[job] as YamlMap)['steps'] as YamlList;
+  return steps
+      .whereType<YamlMap>()
+      .firstWhere((s) => (s['name']?.toString() ?? '') == stepName)['run']
+      .toString();
+}
+
+/// The macOS publish legs and the jobs that must run on fa-m5-1.
+const mobileMacosLegs = <String, List<String>>{
+  '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml': ['build-ios', 'submit-ios'],
+  '.github/workflows/build-macos.yml': ['build-macos'],
+};

+          final runsOn = (jobs[id] as YamlMap)['runs-on'].toString();
+          expect(

+            contains('macos-m5'),
+            reason:

+                '`macos-m5` (the fa-m5-1 registration) — the generic '
+                '`[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` list also matches the Linux '
+                'self-hosted box, and the job ran there with no '
+                'ruby/fastlane/Xcode (gh-1600: exit 127 at Install fastlane)',
+          );

+            runsOn.contains('macOS') || runsOn.contains('ARM64'),
+            isFalse,
+            reason:
+                '$entry.key job "$id" must not carry the generic '
+                '`macOS`/`ARM64` labels — only the unambiguous `macos-m5` '
+                'pin routes to the M5 runner (gh-1600 F-A)',
+          );
+        });
+      }
+    }
+

bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates
          # EMPTY — harbor died with "Dataset  not found" (run 38126875911).
          # DATASET comes from the bench job's env block above
          # (needs.setup.outputs.dataset).
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch is the bench default on EVERY
          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430
          # invariant (never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog +
          # margin — the REG in test_fa_agent_timeout.py reads the Dart
          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'

    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}

    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:

Now the cleanup step: `docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` — this filters containers by NAME containing the job name. blocks.text:
Harbor itself is an external package (`harbor[modal]==0.23.0`). We can't verify the container-naming from the repo. The teardown is best-effort with `|| true`, and the checkout itself is now tolerant, so even if the name filter doesn't match, the workflow no longer breaks. But if the filter never matches, the docker-held leftovers would persist on the box indefinitely and every subsequent mobile checkout would hit the log-and-prune path (warnings, moved-aside stale dirs accumulating in RUNNER_TEMP... actually stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP are never cleaned up either — that's a disk-growth concern on a persistent box. Hmm: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — moved leftovers accumulate in RUNNER_TEMP. RUNNER_TEMP is "cleaned up at the end of each job"? Actually the doc says the directory is cleaned at the end of the job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, the runner does clean RUNNER_TEMP at job end (the runner process does this — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of each job"). Hmm, is that true for self-hosted? The runner app does clean _temp between jobs, yes (Runner.Worker deletes _temp contents post-job). But if the moved-aside stale dir contains a mount stub (unremovable), the runner's cleanup may fail silently, leaving junk. It's a best-effort tradeoff; acceptable but worth a suggestion note (accumulating stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP if the runner's cleanup can't remove mount stubs either).

Also note: since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the start of each job, parking bench output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` is safe per-job.

Wait — but there's a subtle issue with the bench output being in RUNNER_TEMP and the harbor containers bind-mounting trial dirs from there. The trial dirs are bind-mounted into task containers — when the job ends and the runner cleans RUNNER_TEMP while containers still hold the mounts... but the new cleanup step removes the containers BEFORE rm -rf. And rm -rf happens at the end of the job anyway. If a shard is cancelled mid-run: `if: always()` — the cleanup step still runs. Good.

But there's one more subtlety: with RUNNER_TEMP cleanup by the runner itself, the explicit `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` is still useful because the runner's cleanup can fail on mount-held dirs too. Fine.

Now — a REAL potential issue with `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"`: this is a shared path across SHARDS of the same run IF multiple shards run on the same box concurrently. The bench matrix has `max-parallel: 5`. If a `cpu-runner: self-hosted` dispatch routes several shards to the same self-hosted box (single runner registration = one job at a time, so sequential), no concurrent clash. But if the box hosts MULTIPLE runner registrations (common for "the Linux self-hosted box" to have several — bench-mls.yml has 3 self-hosted jobs...). If two shards run concurrently on the same box via two registrations, each job has its own RUNNER_TEMP (per-registration _work/_temp) — actually RUNNER_TEMP = <runner-root>/_temp which is per-registration, not per-job. So two registrations have distinct _temp dirs. OK, no clash.

But wait — if the same registration runs shard A, then (after A's job ends, including the cleanup step) shard B — cleanup already removed bench. Fine.

Now, the artifact upload: `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/jobs/` — upload-artifact v7 with a path outside the workspace — supported (any absolute path). OK.

One thing to verify: the "Upload to Harbor Hub" step has `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. `env.HARBOR_API_KEY` refers to the step's env block — this is pre-existing.

Now the cleanup step runs `if: always()` — note the ordering: it runs AFTER Upload harbor job and Upload to Harbor Hub. Steps run sequentially in order — the cleanup step is declared after the upload steps. Good.

But — hmm, one issue: the cleanup step's docker teardown uses the filter `name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}`. But `matrix.kind` — does the matrix include a `kind` key? In the matrix generated by split_tasks.py. The harbor run step uses `${{ matrix.kind }}` — pre-existing usage, so yes it exists.

Now the KEY question about correctness of the container name filter: harbor job name is `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}` e.g. `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14`. If harbor names containers e.g. `<job-name>-<task>-<attempt>`, the filter matches (name filter is substring/regex match). Harbor 0.23 names task containers... I recall terminal-bench harbor containers are named like `{job_name}--{task_id}--{attempt}` or similar. The name filter would then substring-match. Reasonable. If it doesn't match, best-effort + tolerant checkout covers it. I'll note as a suggestion (verify the filter against actual container names, e.g. add a `docker ps` debug line).

Now build-mobile.yml and build-macos.yml checkout scripts. Let me examine the "clone around stub" logic for a subtle bug:

```bash
CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    name="$(basename "$entry")"
    if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
      echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
    else
      mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
    fi
  done <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
```

Issues:
1. If a stub collision occurs for a top-level entry (e.g. a leftover `jobs/` dir), the fresh `jobs/` content is DELETED by `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` and the stale stub remains. For non-repo paths like `jobs/`, harmless. For repo paths (e.g. a leftover `build/` — wait, build cache is parked first in build-macos; `build/` in build-mobile is a repo path? Let me check if flutter build outputs to build/. Yes — Flutter builds write to `build/`, and the repo may have committed build/ or not. If a stale unremovable `build/` stub exists, the fresh checkout's `build/` would be dropped and the stale one kept — with a warning. Then subsequent build steps would operate on stale build/. This is the last-resort path though; the alternative (fail checkout) is worse. It's documented with a warning. OK — suggestion level at most.

2. `while ... done <(find ...)` — process substitution requires bash; the step uses `shell: bash`? Default for `run` on Linux is bash — fine. `set -euo pipefail` is active. Process substitution failure wouldn't be caught, fine.

3. The `find` loop with `mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"`: moving `.git` — after moving all entries, `git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log` works. Good.

4. Edge: `mv` across same filesystem — CLONE_TARGET is `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout`, a sibling in the same parent dir — same FS. Good.

5. `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` at the start — could delete a leftover `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout` from a previous failed run. Good hygiene.

6. The earlier guard: `if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A ...)" ]` — move-aside. If `mv` fails (mount stub at the top level? no — stub is INSIDE the workspace; the workspace dir itself can't be moved if... the workspace dir can be moved even with a mount stub inside? Moving a directory containing a mount point: rename(2) works for a dir containing mounts? No! rename of a directory that contains a mountpoint fails with EBUSY on Linux (moving a directory subtree containing a mount is not allowed). Actually rename(2) on a directory containing a bind mount fails with EBUSY ("Device or resource busy"). That's exactly why the fallback exists — mv fails → clone-around-stub. Good chain.

7. But — if `mv` succeeded, `$STALE` holds the old tree; then `mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` creates a fresh empty dir; clone goes into it directly (CLONE_TARGET == GITHUB_WORKSPACE since ls -A finds nothing). Fi…

      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"

            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."

          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"

          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"

            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then

          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi

            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"

        run: |

          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin

      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi

Now let me read the full workflow files to check for correctness of the changes in context. Key areas to review:

1. `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` — around lines 560-670
2. `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` — the build-macos job
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` — build-ios and submit-ios jobs

Let me also check:
- Are there other jobs in build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml with `self-hosted` labels? E.g., are there other macOS legs in `daily-publish.yml`, `release-appstore.yml`, `ci.yml`, etc. that still use the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label? The ticket says "Audit other macOS-only legs the same way." Let me grep.
- Also check `RUNNER_TEMP` vs `runner.temp` semantics — in the workflow, `$RUNNER_TEMP` env var is available in run steps. In `if: always()` conditions it would be `${{ runner.temp }}`. Fine.
- Check whether `FAMILY` is in scope in the cleanup step of bench-harbor (it's a job-level env?). Let me check.
- Potential issue: in the cleanup step, `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` removes the whole `/bench` dir — shared between shards? Each job has its own runner temp on the same machine? RUNNER_TEMP is per-job: "The path to a temporary directory on the runner that is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job" — actually RUNNER_TEMP is unique per job run (it's per-runner-process per job). On self-hosted runners, RUNNER_TEMP is something like `/home/runner/work/_temp`, which is shared across concurrent jobs on the same runner machine but unique per job process? Let me think. Actually per GitHub docs: `RUNNER_TEMP` — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job, and is cleaned up at the end of each job... shared between jobs of the same workflow run"? Let me recall precisely: "RUNNER_TEMP: The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of the job. Note: this directory is shared between the jobs of the same workflow run"? Hmm. The official doc says: "RUNNER_TEMP — The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job, and is cleaned up at the end of each job." And there's a note: "This directory is shared between jobs of the same workflow" — no wait.

Actually the docs (docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/variables):
- `RUNNER_TEMP`: "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job, and is cleaned up at the end of the job. Note that this directory is shared between jobs of the same workflow run if they run on the same runner sequentially?" Hmm, I recall there is a note: "This variable is only set for container actions"? Not that.

Let me check the real doc content: "RUNNER_TEMP The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job, and is cleaned up at the end of each job." I believe there IS a note about it being shared between jobs in the same run? Actually I recall: "Note: This directory is shared between jobs of the same workflow run." No — I think that's for `RUNNER_WORKSPACE`. RUNNER_WORKSPACE is shared across jobs of the same workflow run on the same runner. RUNNER_TEMP is per-job.

Hmm, actually from GitHub docs on default environment variables:
- `RUNNER_TEMP`: "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job, and is cleaned up at the end of each job. Note: this directory is shared between the jobs in a workflow run if the jobs run on the same runner." — I'm not 100% sure.

There's a known behavior: on self-hosted runners, RUNNER_TEMP is `<runner-root>/_temp`, and it's cleaned (emptied) between jobs. If two jobs run concurrently on the same runner (can't happen for the same runner registration unless a second registration), they'd share. A single runner registration runs one job at a time.

In bench-harbor, shards run on a matrix — if all shards run on the same self-hosted box sequentially (single registration) or on different boxes, the `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` in the cleanup removes the WHOLE bench dir, not just this shard's subdir. Since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the beginning of each job and cleaned up at the end, and one runner runs one job at a time, this is fine per job. But if the runner box hosts multiple runner registrations (e.g., multiple runners on the same machine), RUNNER_TEMP differs per registration? RUNNER_TEMP is under each runner's own `_work/_temp` typically — per-registration. OK.

But there's a subtle race: `harbor run ... -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` then upload artifact from `${{ runner.temp }}/bench/jobs/`, then "Upload to Harbor Hub" iterates `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs`, then cleanup removes `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench`. Sequential within a job — fine.

One question: does `harbor` docker containers outlive the job? The cleanup `docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` — container names must actually match this pattern. If harbor names containers differently (e.g., includes a run-id or random suffix), the filter may not match. We can't verify harbor's naming from the repo unless harbor source is vendored. Let me check if there's a harbor package in the repo. The comment in the test says trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers. Harbor is an external tool (bench harness). Let me grep for harbor container naming conventions in the repo.

Also key review question: the `submit-ios` job — needs: [build-ios]; both now pinned to `[self-hosted, macos-m5]`. Since there's only ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), build-ios and submit-ios run sequentially on the same box. Good.

But WAIT — a critical thing: if `build-ios` and `submit-ios` both run on the single macOS runner, and there is a concurrency setup with daily-publish, they queue. Fine.

Another important check: are there OTHER jobs across the workflow set that still use `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`? The ticket says "Audit other macOS-only legs the same way." Let me grep for `macOS, ARM64` in .github/workflows.

Also check that `macos-m5` label is actually used elsewhere (gh-1005 convention from ci.yml) — verify the label name spelled the same way in ci.yml.

Potential issues in the diff:

1. In build-macos.yml checkout: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true` — dirname of the STALE path (RUNNER_TEMP) — fine. Then `mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE"`. But GITHUB_WORKSPACE's parent must be writable for rename — the workspace dir is renamed (same filesystem) — fine. If mv succeeds, then `mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` creates a fresh empty dir. If mv fails, mkdir -p keeps existing dir with leftovers, and clone goes to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout`, then move entries around stubs. OK.

2. The move-in loop: `find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` lists entries; `mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"`. Note `find` output paths with spaces — the while read handles whitespace except newlines. Filenames with newlines would break, but repo files don't have newlines. Fine-ish.

3. A subtle issue: after moving entries into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` around a stub, `.git` directory moves — but `git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline` works. OK.

4. However — moving dotfiles: `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` includes dot entries (`.git`), yes, find lists hidden files too. Good.

5. `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` after moving — the leftover colliding entries remain and get removed with the CLONE_TARGET — wait, if a stub collision happened ("left in $CLONE_TARGET"), then `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` deletes the colliding entry — i.e., the newly cloned file that couldn't be moved is deleted. The workspace keeps the STUB version (stale leftover from previous run) — meaning stale content could shadow fresh checkout content! E.g., if leftover `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` is a mount stub in the workspace and the fresh checkout has a `jobs/` path... Actually `jobs/` is not a repo…

bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates
          # EMPTY — harbor died with "Dataset  not found" (run 38126875911).
          # DATASET comes from the bench job's env block above
          # (needs.setup.outputs.dataset).
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch is the bench default on EVERY
          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430
          # invariant (never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog +
          # margin — the REG in test_fa_agent_timeout.py reads the Dart
          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"

          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done

          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"

            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}

blocks.text:
Harbor itself is an external package (`harbor[modal]==0.23.0`). We can't verify the container-naming from the repo. The teardown is best-effort with `|| true`, and the checkout itself is now tolerant, so even if the name filter doesn't match, the workflow no longer breaks. But if the filter never matches, the docker-held leftovers would persist on the box indefinitely and every subsequent mobile checkout would hit the log-and-prune path (warnings, moved-aside stale dirs accumulating in RUNNER_TEMP... actually stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP are never cleaned up either — that's a disk-growth concern on a persistent box. Hmm: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — moved leftovers accumulate in RUNNER_TEMP. RUNNER_TEMP is "cleaned up at the end of each job"? Actually the doc says the directory is cleaned at the end of the job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, the runner does clean RUNNER_TEMP at job end (the runner process does this — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of each job"). Hmm, is that true for self-hosted? The runner app does clean _temp between jobs, yes (Runner.Worker deletes _temp contents post-job). But if the moved-aside stale dir contains a mount stub (unremovable), the runner's cleanup may fail silently, leaving junk. It's a best-effort tradeoff; acceptable but worth a suggestion note (accumulating stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP if the runner's cleanup can't remove mount stubs either).

Also note: since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the start of each job, parking bench output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` is safe per-job.

Wait — but there's a subtle issue with the bench output being in RUNNER_TEMP and the harbor containers bind-mounting trial dirs from there. The trial dirs are bind-mounted into task containers — when the job ends and the runner cleans RUNNER_TEMP while containers still hold the mounts... but the new cleanup step removes the containers BEFORE rm -rf. And rm -rf happens at the end of the job anyway. If a shard is cancelled mid-run: `if: always()` — the cleanup step still runs. Good.

update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then

bench-mls.yml: uses `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.bench-venv` and `PYTHONPATH=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/mls/harbor` — reads from its workspace (checked out by actions/checkout@v4 presumably — on the self-hosted box, actions/checkout... wait — bench-mls jobs run `runs-on: self-hosted` bare. Do they use actions/checkout? If the same shared workspace path is used by bench-mls and bench-harbor and the mobile legs, then actions/checkout on the persistent box also does `rm -rf`-ish cleaning (it runs `git clean -ffq` etc. — actions/checkout on self-hosted does NOT delete the workspace; it reuses the existing repo). bench-mls writing `.bench-venv` INTO the workspace — the mobile mirror-checkout's rm -rf removes it (removable) — fine.

But hmm — one more subtle NEW risk introduced by THIS PR: bench-harbor's bench job previously used `actions/checkout` (line 451: `uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e...`) — the bench job on the self-hosted box uses the SAME $GITHUB_WORKSPACE as the mobile legs. The bench job's harbor output moved OUT of the workspace — good. But the trial CONTAINERS bind-mount trial dirs — now under `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs/<name>/<trial>/`. RUNNER_TEMP on a self-hosted box is `<runner-root>/_temp` — NOT the workspace. Mounts hold `<runner-root>/_temp/bench/...` — outside the workspace, so the mobile checkout's `rm -rf $GITHUB_WORKSPACE` no longer touches them. The cleanup step still tears containers down + rm -rf the bench dir. Good — F-B fully addressed for bench-harbor.

Does the bench job itself still leave anything in the workspace? `.bench-venv` created in workspace (uv venv .bench-venv) — removable, no mounts. The trial containers may ALSO bind-mount the BUNDLE dir or task dirs from the workspace? The `fa-bundle.tar.gz` artifact is downloaded into the workspace, and `FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz` — passed to harbor; the containers probably mount/copy the bundle. If a container bind-mounts the tarball path in the workspace, the mobile checkout's rm would hit an unremovable FILE stub... A bind-mounted FILE can't be unlinked (EBUSY? actually unlinking a bind-mounted file succeeds on Linux — mounts on files: you can rm the name; the inode lives till unmount). Only directories-as-mount-points block rmdir. So workspace leftovers from bundle mounts wouldn't block. And the tolerant checkout covers it anyway. OK.

Now — the `summary` job: `path: jobs` download + `python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY"` — reads downloaded artifacts. Unchanged semantics. Good.

Next: verify there are no other references to the old workspace `jobs/` output dir anywhere (e.g. docs, other workflows reading `harbor-job-shard`). Fine.

Now let me double-check the docker name-filter over-match concern with actual matrix values: matrix.i values — shards 0..15 presumably (`default: '16'`). SHARD=1 filter `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-1` also matches shard `14`, `15` container names (if containers carry the job name as a name prefix). Are harbor's container names derived from the job name? Harbor 0.23 terminal-bench: containers are named like `{job_name}--{task_name}--{attempt}` or `{task}-{attempt}-{job}`? I can't verify externally... Let me try fetching harbor docs quickly? Harbor is `tbench` harbor framework (harbor framework for terminal-bench). Maybe pip package source is on PyPI — I could try web_fetch of the GitHub repo. Let me do a quick search to confirm container naming. It's worth one search for review accuracy.

bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates
          # EMPTY — harbor died with "Dataset  not found" (run 38126875911).
          # DATASET comes from the bench job's env block above
          # (needs.setup.outputs.dataset).
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch is the bench default on EVERY
          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430
          # invariant (never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog +
          # margin — the REG in test_fa_agent_timeout.py reads the Dart
          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi

          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"

          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The

          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)

            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"

            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
