messages.preview: The workflow changes are clear. Now let me verify the tests pass and check formatting/analysis compliance:

blocks.text:
Harbor itself is an external package (`harbor[modal]==0.23.0`). We can't verify the container-naming from the repo. The teardown is best-effort with `|| true`, and the checkout itself is now tolerant, so even if the name filter doesn't match, the workflow no longer breaks. But if the filter never matches, the docker-held leftovers would persist on the box indefinitely and every subsequent mobile checkout would hit the log-and-prune path (warnings, moved-aside stale dirs accumulating in RUNNER_TEMP... actually stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP are never cleaned up either — that's a disk-growth concern on a persistent box. Hmm: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — moved leftovers accumulate in RUNNER_TEMP. RUNNER_TEMP is "cleaned up at the end of each job"? Actually the doc says the directory is cleaned at the end of the job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, the runner does clean RUNNER_TEMP at job end (the runner process does this — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of each job"). Hmm, is that true for self-hosted? The runner app does clean _temp between jobs, yes (Runner.Worker deletes _temp contents post-job). But if the moved-aside stale dir contains a mount stub (unremovable), the runner's cleanup may fail silently, leaving junk. It's a best-effort tradeoff; acceptable but worth a suggestion note (accumulating stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP if the runner's cleanup can't remove mount stubs either).

Also note: since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the start of each job, parking bench output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` is safe per-job.

Wait — but there's a subtle issue with the bench output being in RUNNER_TEMP and the harbor containers bind-mounting trial dirs from there. The trial dirs are bind-mounted into task containers — when the job ends and the runner cleans RUNNER_TEMP while containers still hold the mounts... but the new cleanup step removes the containers BEFORE rm -rf. And rm -rf happens at the end of the job anyway. If a shard is cancelled mid-run: `if: always()` — the cleanup step still runs. Good.

But there's one more subtlety: with RUNNER_TEMP cleanup by the runner itself, the explicit `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` is still useful because the runner's cleanup can fail on mount-held dirs too. Fine.

Now — a REAL potential issue with `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"`: this is a shared path across SHARDS of the same run IF multiple shards run on the same box concurrently. The bench matrix has `max-parallel: 5`. If a `cpu-runner: self-hosted` dispatch routes several shards to the same self-hosted box (single runner registration = one job at a time, so sequential), no concurrent clash. But if the box hosts MULTIPLE runner registrations (common for "the Linux self-hosted box" to have several — bench-mls.yml has 3 self-hosted jobs...). If two shards run concurrently on the same box via two registrations, each job has its own RUNNER_TEMP (per-registration _work/_temp) — actually RUNNER_TEMP = <runner-root>/_temp which is per-registration, not per-job. So two registrations have distinct _temp dirs. OK, no clash.

But wait — if the same registration runs shard A, then (after A's job ends, including the cleanup step) shard B — cleanup already removed bench. Fine.

Now, the artifact upload: `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/jobs/` — upload-artifact v7 with a path outside the workspace — supported (any absolute path). OK.

One thing to verify: the "Upload to Harbor Hub" step has `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. `env.HARBOR_API_KEY` refers to the step's env block — this is pre-existing.

Now the cleanup step runs `if: always()` — note the ordering: it runs AFTER Upload harbor job and Upload to Harbor Hub. Steps run sequentially in order — the cleanup step is declared after the upload steps. Good.

But — hmm, one issue: the cleanup step's docker teardown uses the filter `name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}`. But `matrix.kind` — does the matrix include a `kind` key? In the matrix generated by split_tasks.py. The harbor run step uses `${{ matrix.kind }}` — pre-existing usage, so yes it exists.

Now the KEY question about correctness of the container name filter: harbor job name is `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}` e.g. `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14`. If harbor names containers e.g. `<job-name>-<task>-<attempt>`, the filter matches (name filter is substring/regex match). Harbor 0.23 names task containers... I recall terminal-bench harbor containers are named like `{job_name}--{task_id}--{attempt}` or similar. The name filter would then substring-match. Reasonable. If it doesn't match, best-effort + tolerant checkout covers it. I'll note as a suggestion (verify the filter against actual container names, e.g. add a `docker ps` debug line).

Now build-mobile.yml and build-macos.yml checkout scripts. Let me examine the "clone around stub" logic for a subtle bug:

```bash
CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    name="$(basename "$entry")"
    if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
      echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
    else
      mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
    fi
  done <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
```

Issues:

update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip
          # against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv — a wildcard pin
          # re-resolves a new engine build on every 3.47.x patch and moves
          # the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the gate tracks. Bump
          # consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Install Rust toolchain

          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then

            rustup show

            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"

      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"

            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then

          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

messages.preview: The workflow changes are clear. Now let me verify the tests pass and check formatting/analysis compliance:

blocks.text:
Harbor itself is an external package (`harbor[modal]==0.23.0`). We can't verify the container-naming from the repo. The teardown is best-effort with `|| true`, and the checkout itself is now tolerant, so even if the name filter doesn't match, the workflow no longer breaks. But if the filter never matches, the docker-held leftovers would persist on the box indefinitely and every subsequent mobile checkout would hit the log-and-prune path (warnings, moved-aside stale dirs accumulating in RUNNER_TEMP... actually stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP are never cleaned up either — that's a disk-growth concern on a persistent box. Hmm: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — moved leftovers accumulate in RUNNER_TEMP. RUNNER_TEMP is "cleaned up at the end of each job"? Actually the doc says the directory is cleaned at the end of the job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, the runner does clean RUNNER_TEMP at job end (the runner process does this — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of each job"). Hmm, is that true for self-hosted? The runner app does clean _temp between jobs, yes (Runner.Worker deletes _temp contents post-job). But if the moved-aside stale dir contains a mount stub (unremovable), the runner's cleanup may fail silently, leaving junk. It's a best-effort tradeoff; acceptable but worth a suggestion note (accumulating stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP if the runner's cleanup can't remove mount stubs either).

Also note: since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the start of each job, parking bench output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` is safe per-job.

Wait — but there's a subtle issue with the bench output being in RUNNER_TEMP and the harbor containers bind-mounting trial dirs from there. The trial dirs are bind-mounted into task containers — when the job ends and the runner cleans RUNNER_TEMP while containers still hold the mounts... but the new cleanup step removes the containers BEFORE rm -rf. And rm -rf happens at the end of the job anyway. If a shard is cancelled mid-run: `if: always()` — the cleanup step still runs. Good.

But there's one more subtlety: with RUNNER_TEMP cleanup by the runner itself, the explicit `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` is still useful because the runner's cleanup can fail on mount-held dirs too. Fine.

Now — a REAL potential issue with `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"`: this is a shared path across SHARDS of the same run IF multiple shards run on the same box concurrently. The bench matrix has `max-parallel: 5`. If a `cpu-runner: self-hosted` dispatch routes several shards to the same self-hosted box (single runner registration = one job at a time, so sequential), no concurrent clash. But if the box hosts MULTIPLE runner registrations (common for "the Linux self-hosted box" to have several — bench-mls.yml has 3 self-hosted jobs...). If two shards run concurrently on the same box via two registrations, each job has its own RUNNER_TEMP (per-registration _work/_temp) — actually RUNNER_TEMP = <runner-root>/_temp which is per-registration, not per-job. So two registrations have distinct _temp dirs. OK, no clash.

But wait — if the same registration runs shard A, then (after A's job ends, including the cleanup step) shard B — cleanup already removed bench. Fine.

Now, the artifact upload: `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/jobs/` — upload-artifact v7 with a path outside the workspace — supported (any absolute path). OK.

One thing to verify: the "Upload to Harbor Hub" step has `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. `env.HARBOR_API_KEY` refers to the step's env block — this is pre-existing.

Now the cleanup step runs `if: always()` — note the ordering: it runs AFTER Upload harbor job and Upload to Harbor Hub. Steps run sequentially in order — the cleanup step is declared after the upload steps. Good.

But — hmm, one issue: the cleanup step's docker teardown uses the filter `name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}`. But `matrix.kind` — does the matrix include a `kind` key? In the matrix generated by split_tasks.py. The harbor run step uses `${{ matrix.kind }}` — pre-existing usage, so yes it exists.

Now the KEY question about correctness of the container name filter: harbor job name is `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}` e.g. `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14`. If harbor names containers e.g. `<job-name>-<task>-<attempt>`, the filter matches (name filter is substring/regex match). Harbor 0.23 names task containers... I recall terminal-bench harbor containers are named like `{job_name}--{task_id}--{attempt}` or similar. The name filter would then substring-match. Reasonable. If it doesn't match, best-effort + tolerant checkout covers it. I'll note as a suggestion (verify the filter against actual container names, e.g. add a `docker ps` debug line).

Now build-mobile.yml and build-macos.yml checkout scripts. Let me examine the "clone around stub" logic for a subtle bug:

```bash
CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    name="$(basename "$entry")"
    if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
      echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
    else
      mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
    fi
  done <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
```

Issues:
1. If a stub collision occurs for a top-level entry (e.g. a leftover `jobs/` dir), the fresh `jobs/` content is DELETED by `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` and the stale stub remains. update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip
          # against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv — a wildcard pin
          # re-resolves a new engine build on every 3.47.x patch and moves
          # the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the gate tracks. Bump
          # consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Install Rust toolchain

          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then

            rustup show

            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"

      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"

            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then

          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

messages.preview: The workflow changes are clear. Now let me verify the tests pass and check formatting/analysis compliance:

blocks.text:
Harbor itself is an external package (`harbor[modal]==0.23.0`). We can't verify the container-naming from the repo. The teardown is best-effort with `|| true`, and the checkout itself is now tolerant, so even if the name filter doesn't match, the workflow no longer breaks. But if the filter never matches, the docker-held leftovers would persist on the box indefinitely and every subsequent mobile checkout would hit the log-and-prune path (warnings, moved-aside stale dirs accumulating in RUNNER_TEMP... actually stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP are never cleaned up either — that's a disk-growth concern on a persistent box. Hmm: `STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"` — moved leftovers accumulate in RUNNER_TEMP. RUNNER_TEMP is "cleaned up at the end of each job"? Actually the doc says the directory is cleaned at the end of the job on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, the runner does clean RUNNER_TEMP at job end (the runner process does this — "The path to a temporary directory on the runner. This directory is guaranteed to be empty at the beginning of each job and is cleaned at the end of each job"). Hmm, is that true for self-hosted? The runner app does clean _temp between jobs, yes (Runner.Worker deletes _temp contents post-job). But if the moved-aside stale dir contains a mount stub (unremovable), the runner's cleanup may fail silently, leaving junk. It's a best-effort tradeoff; acceptable but worth a suggestion note (accumulating stale-workspace dirs in RUNNER_TEMP if the runner's cleanup can't remove mount stubs either).

Also note: since RUNNER_TEMP is guaranteed empty at the start of each job, parking bench output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` is safe per-job.

Wait — but there's a subtle issue with the bench output being in RUNNER_TEMP and the harbor containers bind-mounting trial dirs from there. The trial dirs are bind-mounted into task containers — when the job ends and the runner cleans RUNNER_TEMP while containers still hold the mounts... but the new cleanup step removes the containers BEFORE rm -rf. And rm -rf happens at the end of the job anyway. If a shard is cancelled mid-run: `if: always()` — the cleanup step still runs. Good.

But there's one more subtlety: with RUNNER_TEMP cleanup by the runner itself, the explicit `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` is still useful because the runner's cleanup can fail on mount-held dirs too. Fine.

Now — a REAL potential issue with `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"`: this is a shared path across SHARDS of the same run IF multiple shards run on the same box concurrently. The bench matrix has `max-parallel: 5`. If a `cpu-runner: self-hosted` dispatch routes several shards to the same self-hosted box (single runner registration = one job at a time, so sequential), no concurrent clash. But if the box hosts MULTIPLE runner registrations (common for "the Linux self-hosted box" to have several — bench-mls.yml has 3 self-hosted jobs...). If two shards run concurrently on the same box via two registrations, each job has its own RUNNER_TEMP (per-registration _work/_temp) — actually RUNNER_TEMP = <runner-root>/_temp which is per-registration, not per-job. So two registrations have distinct _temp dirs. OK, no clash.

But wait — if the same registration runs shard A, then (after A's job ends, including the cleanup step) shard B — cleanup already removed bench. Fine.

Now, the artifact upload: `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/jobs/` — upload-artifact v7 with a path outside the workspace — supported (any absolute path). OK.

One thing to verify: the "Upload to Harbor Hub" step has `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. `env.HARBOR_API_KEY` refers to the step's env block — this is pre-existing.

Now the cleanup step runs `if: always()` — note the ordering: it runs AFTER Upload harbor job and Upload to Harbor Hub. Steps run sequentially in order — the cleanup step is declared after the upload steps. Good.

But — hmm, one issue: the cleanup step's docker teardown uses the filter `name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}`. But `matrix.kind` — does the matrix include a `kind` key? In the matrix generated by split_tasks.py. The harbor run step uses `${{ matrix.kind }}` — pre-existing usage, so yes it exists.

Now the KEY question about correctness of the container name filter: harbor job name is `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}` e.g. `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14`. If harbor names containers e.g. `<job-name>-<task>-<attempt>`, the filter matches (name filter is substring/regex match). Harbor 0.23 names task containers... I recall terminal-bench harbor containers are named like `{job_name}--{task_id}--{attempt}` or similar. The name filter would then substring-match. Reasonable. If it doesn't match, best-effort + tolerant checkout covers it. I'll note as a suggestion (verify the filter against actual container names, e.g. add a `docker ps` debug line).

Now build-mobile.yml and build-macos.yml checkout scripts. Let me examine the "clone around stub" logic for a subtle bug:

```bash
CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    name="$(basename "$entry")"
    if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
      echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
    else
      mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
    fi
  done <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
  rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
fi
echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
```

Issues:
1. If a stub collision occurs for a top-level entry (e.g. a leftover `jobs/` dir), the fresh `jobs/` content is DELETED by `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` and the stale stub remains. For non-repo paths like `jobs/`, harmless. For repo paths (e.g. a leftover `build/` — wait, build cache is parked first in build-macos; `build/` in build-mobile is a repo path? Let me check if flutter build outputs to build/. Yes — Flutter builds write to `build/`, and the repo may have committed build/ or not. If a stale unremovable `build/` stub exists, the fresh checkout's `build/` would be dropped and the stale one kept — with a warning. Then subsequent build steps would operate on stale build/. update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the

      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:

      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then

            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"

But wait — is this scenario realistic on the actual runner? On the self-hosted box, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` = `<runner>/_work/<repo>/<repo>` and the parent `<repo>` is owned by the runner user — writable. The move-aside would only fail there because of a mount-held path issue: rename(2) of a directory CONTAING a mount point fails with EBUSY even with writable parent. In THAT realistic case, creating `workspace.checkout` in the writable parent succeeds, and the clone-around works.

So the failure mode I simulated (unwritable parent) is not the realistic failure mode. Let me re-simulate with the REALISTIC stub: a directory that can't be deleted/moved because it's a mount point. I can't create real mounts without privileges... but I CAN simulate EBUSY by making the leftover path a mount-like obstacle: use `chattr +i`? With parent writable and a leftover chmod-000 dir inside, mv of the whole workspace SUCCEEDS (dir modes don't block rename). So the only realistic mv-failure is a mount point inside the workspace (EBUSY) or unwritable parent.

For the mount-point case, the `.checkout` sibling IS creatable (parent writable), so the clone-around works. My simulated unwritable-parent case is a different, unusual failure mode.

BUT — there's still a genuine latent issue worth flagging: in the clone-around path, if `git clone` fails to create `$CLONE_TARGET` for ANY reason, the checkout fails (set -e) — which is fine/expected (a genuine failure should fail). The deeper issue: **the workspace tree the clone falls back into is INCOMPLETE**. Consider the realistic mount-stub case, which I should verify works. Let me check `id -u` and try mounting a tmpfs. If unprivileged, an alternative: use a read-only bind? Not without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

Alternative realistic simulation: make the leftover a FIFO or a... no. Actually there's another way mv fails with writable parent: the workspace dir itself is on a different filesystem than STALE? No — mv falls back to copy+delete across FS, but STALE is in RUNNER_TEMP which may be a DIFFERENT filesystem than _work! mv across devices = copy + rm -rf source. If source contains an undeletable mount, the rm part fails but mv has already COPIED. Actually mv would copy, then fail removing... coreutils mv: cross-device move of a dir = copy then remove source; if remove fails, mv reports error and exits non-zero, leaving the copy in STALE AND the source in place. So the REAL failing branch I found requires an unwritable parent — unusual on the runner (the runner user owns _work).       github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      # gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on this persistent box is SHARED across
      # workflow runs — the old bare workspace rm -rf failed the checkout on
      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) via its
    # unique registration label. The old generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # list also matched the Linux self-hosted box's labels, and this job ran
    # there — no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127;
    # later steps died on `security: command not found`).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      # gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on this persistent box is SHARED across
      # workflow runs — the old bare workspace rm -rf failed the checkout on
      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB

- clean clone (empty workspace)
- workspace with REMOVABLE leftovers → first rm -rf succeeds (exit 0)... wait, `if ! rm -rf ...` — when rm succeeds, no warnings, workspace gone, mkdir fresh, clone directly. Good.

{"path":"/tmp/sim_checkout.sh","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (build-mobile.yml
# build-ios/submit-ios + build-macos.yml build-macos), per scenario.
set -uo pipefail

SCEN="$1"; shift
ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"
export GITHUB_WORKSPACE="$ROOT/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness"
export RUNNER_TEMP="$ROOT/runner_temp"
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP"

# git stub: simulates clone (creates target with .git + tracked file) + log
mkdir -p "$ROOT/bin"
cat > "$ROOT/bin/git" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "clone" ]; then
  shift; shift # --reference arg
  shift        # mirror path
  shift; shift # --depth=1
  url="$1"; target="$2"
  mkdir -p "$target/.git" "$target/lib"
  echo "ref: refs/heads/main" > "$target/.git/HEAD"
  echo "tracked file" > "$target/lib/main.dart"
  echo "Cloning into '$target'"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$1" = "-C" ]; then
  dir="$2"; shift 2
  if [ "$1" = "log" ]; then
    [ -d "$dir/.git" ] || { echo "fatal: not a git repository: $dir" >&2; exit 128; }
    echo "abc1234 simulated HEAD"
    exit 0
  fi
fi
echo "git-stub: unhandled $*" >&2
exit 1
EOF
chmod +x "$ROOT/bin/git"
export PATH="$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

MIRROR="$ROOT/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
mkdir -p "$MIRROR"
cd /tmp

# ── build the exact committed script for the requested workflow/job ──
python3 - "$SCEN" "$ROOT/script.sh" <<'PYEOF'
import sys, yaml
scen, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
wf, job = {
    'mobile-ios': ('.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml', 'build-ios'),
    'macos': ('.github/workflows/build-macos.yml', 'build-macos'),
}[scen]
doc = yaml.safe_load(open('/home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness/' + wf))
steps = doc['jobs'][job]['steps']
name = 'Checkout repository from local mirror' if 'mobile' in scen else 'Checkout repository from local mirrors'
script = next(s['run'] for s in steps if s.get('name') == name)
open(out, 'w').write(script)
PYEOF

# ARCH/BUILD_CACHE_DIR for the macos scenario are set inside the script itself.
export ARCH="arm64"

case "$SCEN" in
  mobile-ios)
    ;;
  macos)
    ;;
esac

echo "=== SCENARIO: $SCEN ==="
case "$2" in
esac

run_case() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  echo "--- case: $label ---"
  bash "$ROOT/script.sh" >/tmp/sim_out.txt 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  echo "exit=$rc"
  cat /tmp/sim_out.txt
  echo "workspace listing:"
  ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo
}

case "$1" in
  clean)
    mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
    run_case "clean clone (empty workspace)"
    [ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/lib/main.dart" ] && echo "PASS: tracked file present" || echo "FAIL"
    ;;
  removable-leftover)
    mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14"
    echo junk > "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/t.sqlite"
    run_case "removable leftovers"
    [ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/lib/main.dart" ] && [ ! -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs" ] && echo "PASS: leftovers gone, fresh clone in place" || echo "FAIL"
    ;;
  unremovable-leftover)
    # leftover dir made undeletable (no write permission) -> rm -rf fails
    mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14"
    echo junk > "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/t.sqlite"
    chmod 000 "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14"
    run_case "unremovable leftover (move-aside path)"
    chmod 755 "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../flutter_agent_harness/../.." 2>/dev/null
    chmod 755 "$ROOT/runner_temp"/stale-workspace-*/* 2>/dev/null
    [ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/lib/main.dart" ] && echo "PASS: fresh clone, leftover moved aside" || echo "FAIL"
    ls -A "$RUNNER_TEMP" | sed 's/^/  RUNNER_TEMP: /'

    chmod 755 "$PARENT"
    [ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/lib/main.dart" ] && echo "PASS: cloned around stub" || echo "FAIL"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "unknown case $1"; exit 64;;
esac

messages.preview: The clone-around fallback fails when the workspace's PARENT is unwritable — let me check if that's realistic on the actual runner and try to simulate the true mount-stub (EBUSY) case:

blocks.text:
IMPORTANT FINDING! The clone-around-stub fallback has a real bug:

When the workspace dir cannot be MOVED ASIDE because its PARENT directory is not writable (`mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE"` fails with Permission denied on the parent), the script falls into the clone-around path, choosing `CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"` — a SIBLING in the SAME unwritable parent. Creating that sibling fails with `mkdir: Permission denied` (git clone can't create the target dir) → the whole checkout FAILS.

But wait — is this scenario realistic on the actual runner? On the self-hosted box, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` = `<runner>/_work/<repo>/<repo>` and the parent `<repo>` is owned by the runner user — writable. The move-aside would only fail there because of a mount-held path issue: rename(2) of a directory CONTAING a mount point fails with EBUSY even with writable parent. In THAT realistic case, creating `workspace.checkout` in the writable parent succeeds, and the clone-around works.

So the failure mode I simulated (unwritable parent) is not the realistic failure mode. Let me re-simulate with the REALISTIC stub: a directory that can't be deleted/moved because it's a mount point. I can't create real mounts without privileges... but I CAN simulate EBUSY by making the leftover path a mount-like obstacle: use `chattr +i`? Needs CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE — may work as root in this container? Let me check if I'm root.

Actually, a simpler realistic simulation: make the workspace itself contain an undeletable entry AND the parent writable but... mv of the workspace dir: rename(2) needs write perm on parent only (plus the dir must not be ancestor of the cwd etc.). With parent writable and a leftover chmod-000 dir inside, mv of the whole workspace SUCCEEDS (dir modes don't block rename).           if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip

Therefore `docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` matches **nothing**. The new cleanup step's docker teardown is a guaranteed no-op. The `rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"` will then fail whenever a leaked container still holds the trial dirs (warning only). Consequences:

1. The docker-teardown REG test (`docker rm -f` before `rm -rf`) passes while the teardown never tears anything down — a false safety net (test asserts shape, not effect — inherent to static tests, fine, but the implementation should actually work).
2. Residual risk to the PUBLISH legs: NONE directly — the trial dirs moved OUT of the workspace, so a leaked container holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/...` no longer blocks the mobile checkout. The tolerant checkout covers any residual workspace pollution too.
3. Residual harm: leaked containers (cancelled shard) keep RUNNING on the box consuming CPU/memory until manually removed, and hold `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` so the runner's temp cleanup can't remove it either → disk growth. And per the PR's own story, "a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial containers alive on the persistent box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's workspace clean fail" — with the output moved out of the workspace, the hold no longer breaks the next workflow, but the leaked containers persist.

      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a

      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)

          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no

      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies

      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.

            import json, pathlib
            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
            p = next((q for q in cfg["packages"] if q["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"), None)
            print(p["rootUri"] if p else "")

run: flutter test test/integration/mobile_channel_it.dart --tags integration

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) via its
    # unique registration label. The old generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # list also matched the Linux self-hosted box's labels, and this job ran
    # there — no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127;
    # later steps died on `security: command not found`).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      # gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on this persistent box is SHARED across
      # workflow runs — the old bare workspace rm -rf failed the checkout on
      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from harbor.models.task.step_name import validate_step_name

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from harbor.models.task.config import TaskOS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EnvironmentPaths:
    """
    Static paths used within the environment.

    Linux containers use POSIX paths (``/logs``, ``/tests``, ``/solution``).
    Windows containers use drive-prefixed paths (``C:/logs``, etc.) — create
    them via :meth:`for_windows` or :meth:`for_os`.

    Environment mount structure:
    /
    └── logs/
        ├── agent/       # Mounted from trial_dir/agent/
        ├── user-agent/  # Mounted from trial_dir/user-agent/ (simulated-user
        │                  trials only; absent otherwise).
        ├── verifier/    # Mounted from trial_dir/verifier/
        └── artifacts/   # Mounted from trial_dir/artifacts/

    Environment copy structure:
    /
    ├── solution/       # Copied over by the OracleAgent only.
    │   ├── solve.{sh,ps1,cmd,bat}
    │   └── ...
    ├── tests/          # Copied over by the Verifier after the agent runs.
        ├── test.{sh,ps1,cmd,bat}
        └── ...
    """

    logs_dir: PurePosixPath = PurePosixPath("/logs")
    agent_dir: PurePosixPath = logs_dir / "agent"
    user_agent_dir: PurePosixPath = logs_dir / "user-agent"
    verifier_dir: PurePosixPath = logs_dir / "verifier"
    artifacts_dir: PurePosixPath = logs_dir / "artifacts"
    tests_dir: PurePosixPath = PurePosixPath("/tests")
    solution_dir: PurePosixPath = PurePosixPath("/solution")
    default_skills_dir: PurePosixPath = PurePosixPath("/harbor/skills")
    reward_text_path: PurePosixPath = verifier_dir / "reward.txt"
    reward_json_path: PurePosixPath = verifier_dir / "reward.json"

    @classmethod
    def for_windows(cls) -> "EnvironmentPaths":
        """Create paths for Windows containers (C: drive prefix)."""
        return cls._with_root(PurePosixPath("C:/"))

    @classmethod
    def for_os(cls, os: "TaskOS") -> "EnvironmentPaths":
        """Create paths appropriate for the given target OS."""
        # Local import to avoid a circular dependency with task.config.
        from harbor.models.task.config import TaskOS

        if os == TaskOS.WINDOWS:
            return cls.for_windows()
        return cls()

    @classmethod
    def _with_root(cls, root: PurePosixPath) -> "EnvironmentPaths":
        """Create an ``EnvironmentPaths`` rooted at *root* instead of ``/``."""
        logs_dir = root / "logs"
        verifier_dir = logs_dir / "verifier"
        return cls(
            logs_dir=logs_dir,
            agent_dir=logs_dir / "agent",
            user_agent_dir=logs_dir / "user-agent",
            verifier_dir=verifier_dir,
            artifacts_dir=logs_dir / "artifacts",
            tests_dir=root / "tests",
            solution_dir=root / "solution",
            default_skills_dir=root / "harbor" / "skills",
            reward_text_path=verifier_dir / "reward.txt",
            reward_json_path=verifier_dir / "reward.json",
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)

IMPORTANT FINDING! The clone-around-stub fallback has a real bug:

When the workspace dir cannot be MOVED ASIDE because its PARENT directory is not writable (`mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE"` fails with Permission denied on the parent), the script falls into the clone-around path, choosing `CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"` — a SIBLING in the SAME unwritable parent. Creating that sibling fails with `mkdir: Permission denied` (git clone can't create the target dir) → the whole checkout FAILS.

But wait — is this scenario realistic on the actual runner? On the self-hosted box, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` = `<runner>/_work/<repo>/<repo>` and the parent `<repo>` is owned by the runner user — writable. The move-aside would only fail there because of a mount-held path issue: rename(2) of a directory CONTAING a mount point fails with EBUSY even with writable parent. In THAT realistic case, creating `workspace.checkout` in the writable parent succeeds, and the clone-around works.

So the failure mode I simulated (unwritable parent) is not the realistic failure mode. Let me re-simulate with the REALISTIC stub: a directory that can't be deleted/moved because it's a mount point. I can't create real mounts without privileges... but I CAN simulate EBUSY by making the leftover path a mount-like obstacle: use `chattr +i`? Needs CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE — may work as root in this container? Let me check if I'm root.

Actually, a simpler realistic simulation: make the workspace itself contain an undeletable entry AND the parent writable but... mv of the workspace dir: rename(2) needs write perm on parent only (plus the dir must not be ancestor of the cwd etc.). With parent writable and a leftover chmod-000 dir inside, mv of the whole workspace SUCCEEDS (dir modes don't block rename). So the only realistic mv-failure is a mount point inside the workspace (EBUSY) or unwritable parent.

For the mount-point case, the `.checkout` sibling IS creatable (parent writable), so the clone-around works. My simulated unwritable-parent case is a different, unusual failure mode.

BUT — there's still a genuine latent issue worth flagging: in the clone-around path, if `git clone` fails to create `$CLONE_TARGET` for ANY reason, the checkout fails (set -e) — which is fine/expected (a genuine failure should fail). The deeper issue: **the workspace tree the clone falls back into is INCOMPLETE**. Consider the realistic mount-stub case, which I should verify works. Let me check `id -u` and try mounting a tmpfs. If unprivileged, an alternative: use a read-only bind? Not without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

No — mv falls back to copy+delete across FS, but STALE is in RUNNER_TEMP which may be a DIFFERENT filesystem than _work! mv across devices = copy + rm -rf source. If source contains an undeletable mount, the rm part fails but mv has already COPIED. Actually mv would copy, then fail removing... coreutils mv: cross-device move of a dir = copy then remove source; if remove fails, mv reports error and exits non-zero, leaving the copy in STALE AND the source in place. Then: workspace still non-empty → clone-around path → works (parent writable). Leftover stays in workspace forever but checkout proceeds. Fine.
