# gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

**Verified fixed (3 of 4 threads):** the stub-collision inversion (stale stub parked into the `$STALE` sidecar, fresh entry always wins — all 3 checkout scripts), the `stale-workspace-*` pre-prune before each new sidecar, and the repo-wide label audit are all demonstrably in-tree; 13/13 REG tests pass; the reworked checkout paths re-simulated clean.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"
